keyboard/BY.transport: navigator.deviceHandler.sendCommand, hpe command table (M HUB purify.es)
keyboard/BY.coverage: driven live through the native Vue configurator against a fake K99: wired reads 0x87/0x83/0x84/0x8a observed, setPerformance and setReset captured in full; no hardware involved

paths.name: setReset
paths.why: traced from the restoreFactorySetting UI action through the dispatcher to sendCommand('set','setReset',...), and its full 519-byte wired frame is captured -- produced by the vendor's own confirmation dialog against a fake device, so nobody had to send one to a keyboard
paths.sequence: the confirm handler emits 0x04 (setReset) and then 0x0a, 0x06 and three 0x03 frames; only the first is setReset

paths.name: setPerformance
paths.why: same wired lead byte 0x04 as setReset and built by literally the same parser function j_(!0); nothing in the frame shape separates them
paths.proof: A routine setPerformance frame and the factory-reset frame were captured in one session through the vendor's own UI and are BYTE-IDENTICAL across all 519 bytes. The reset's data is the constant x8[model].otherObj -- the factory default performance record -- and that value is reachable from the settings UI, because it is simply what a factory-fresh keyboard reports. Toggling one switch off and back on reproduced it exactly.
paths.consequence: No classifier reading a wired 0x04 frame can separate a settings write from a factory reset. Safety for this path CANNOT be enforced by frame inspection; it has to be enforced at the point of intent -- which command is being issued -- and a captured 0x04 frame must never be replayed.

paths.name: setKeySetting / setMacro / setDiyLight / setLightColor

keyboard/CZ.transport: CZ SDK envelope, report id 0, 64-byte packet, leading 0x55

structural_finding.claim: a CZ read and a CZ write of an all-zero payload are BYTE-IDENTICAL
structural_finding.why: byte 4 carries 'bytes requested' in _simpleGetCommand and 'bytes supplied' in _simpleFullSendCommand; the frame does not distinguish them
structural_finding.asymmetry: The inference runs one way only. The read builder never places bytes after the 8-byte header, so a non-zero trailing region proves a WRITE. An all-zero trailing region proves nothing.
structural_finding.same_shape_as: the BY wired-0x04 ambiguity -- two independent families, two independent instances of the same trap, neither informing the other

keyboard/CZ.command_number_collision_warning: CZ command 0x04 is getBase. BY's wired lead byte 0x04 is setPerformance/setReset. The number is a coincidence across two unrelated families and carries no connection.
